about: Hermann J. Wiemer is best known for Riesling, but the Seneca Lake estate he founded in 1979 has become one of the most respected sources of Finger Lakes Cabernet Franc. In 1998 Wiemer bought two vineyards near Dresden, farther north on the lake’s west shore, and named them Josef and Magdalena. Fred Merwarth and Oskar Bynke, who took over the winery in 2007, now farm them without herbicides alongside the original HJW Vineyard.

Magdalena is a 2.5-acre plot, and the winery calls it its ripest site. The Cabernet Franc vines there were planted in 2004. The grapes are picked and sorted by hand; in 2023 the picks were October 13 and 25. They are destemmed with about a quarter left as whole clusters and fermented with wild yeasts. The wine then ages about 11 months, mostly in neutral 225-liter French barrels and 500-liter Hungarian puncheons with a portion in steel, before bottling without fining.

The winery describes dark fruit and herbal aromas, firm tannins up front and a medium body that opens into black cherry, red plum and spiced cranberry. Wine Advocate found it darker-fruited than the estate’s regular Cabernet Franc. James Suckling noted black cherry, lemon peel, spice and flint, and said it was already showing beautifully. The winery expects it to age well, and it suggests serving it with pork belly or lamb chops.
facts: Wild-yeast fermentation with 25% whole clusters; unfined
About 11 months in neutral 225 l French oak and 500 l Hungarian puncheons, with some stainless steel
